title: Versioned telemetry handshake, rollforward policy, and client-side graceful degradation
creator: Mateo Ruiz
description:
Goal:
Ship a pragmatic, backwards- and forwards-compatible telemetry versioning handshake so SDK, CLI, and server components can safely roll forward to new analytic event shapes without causing application errors or data loss. Provide a documented rollforward policy and client-side graceful degradation behaviors for unsupported fields.

Background:
- Our current telemetry ingestion pipeline rejects events that don't match the active envelope schema, which has caused spikes in telemetry errors after device/SDK upgrades.
- Existing tickets focus on schema negotiation at the gateway layer, but we need an explicit client-server handshake, runtime feature gating, and a safe rollforward strategy so SDKs can emit richer telemetry while receivers can opt-in to consume new fields.
- Stakeholders: Console backend, SDK teams (js/py/go), CLI team, Data infra (analytics ingestion), Product (Console observability).

Proposed design (high level):
1) Versioned envelope header: every telemetry event MUST include a minimal header: {"schema_version": "semver", "compat": "minor|major|experimental", "emitter": "sdk-js-2.5.0"}. The header is optional for legacy clients but required for new SDKs.
2) Handshake endpoint: introduce /telemetry/handshake (lightweight GET) where collectors expose supported schema_version ranges and supported experimental flags per route. SDKs/CLI call handshake at startup or on periodic backoff.
3) Rollforward policy: collectors declare a rollforward window (e.g., accept client minor versions within +1 minor) and explicit opt-in for major/experimental fields. If collector doesn't support a field, it will silently ignore unknown keys.
4) Client-side graceful degradation: SDKs MUST follow a 3-tier behavior when sending unknown fields:
   - If compat=="minor": include field and mark envelope header; proceed normally.
   - If compat=="experimental": include only if handshake indicates experimental_enabled true; otherwise drop field and emit a telemetry diagnostic counter.
   - If compat=="major": do NOT send the field unless handshake explicitly lists supported_major_versions.
5) Fallback envelopes: introduce a lightweight legacy_envelope fallback which strips unknown keys and includes a small manifest so downstream analytics pipelines can attribute missing fields to client versions.

Compatibility matrix (summary):
- Old collectors (pre-handshake): accept legacy_envelope only; SDKs will detect absence of handshake and downgrade to legacy_envelope automatically.
- Collectors with handshake v1: accept legacy_envelope + versioned_envelope up to N minor; will return supported ranges at /telemetry/handshake.
- SDKs 2.x+: prefer versioned_envelope, support graceful degradation logic and handshake.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (Canary): Deploy handshake endpoint to a single ingestion shard and update internal SDK builds to call handshake. Monitor: schema_reject_rate, handshake_error_rate, telemetry_ingest_latency, per-emitter rejected-fields metric. (2 weeks)
- Phase 1 (Hybrid): Gradually enable handshake region-wide and start accepting versioned_envelope with rollforward window of +0 minors. Update CLI canaries. (2 weeks)
- Phase 2 (Rollforward): Expand rollforward window to +1 minor; enable experimental flag gates for a small customer cohort via console flags. (3 weeks)
- Phase 3 (Wide): Default rollforward policy across regions; deprecate critical legacy fields after 90 days with analytics-driven decision.

Validation & QA:
- Unit tests for SDKs that simulate absent handshake and assert envelope fallback.
- Integration test harness that spins collector (handshake enabled/disabled) and runs end-to-end events through ingestion pipeline, asserting no drops and correct attribution.
- Load test with mixed-version emitters to ensure handshake doesn't add significant latency (<5ms p95 additional).
- Data quality checks in Warehouse: weekly dashboards showing per-version field presence heatmaps and missing-field attribution.

Observability & dashboards (owners):
- Telemetry team to add dashboards: handshake_success_rate, handshake_latency_p50/p95, mismatched_schema_rate, legacy_envelope_rate by emitter version. (Owner: Priya Menon)
- Console product to monitor user-visible regressions (Console UX signals) and link regressions to telemetry schema changes. (Owner: Omar Wong)

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Why handshake vs. feature-flag only: handshake provides dynamic server-driven capability discovery for many collectors (multi-region, multi-tenant) without shipping new SDK versions for each collector change.
- Cost: handshake introduces small traffic and storage overhead; mitigated by caching handshake responses in SDKs for 24h and server-side TTL.
- Complexity: SDKs must implement degradation logic; initial engineering cost but reduces ingestion incidents long-term.

Review feedback received so far:
- SEV review (2025-01-28, comments by Linh Tran): insist that collectors default to ignoring unknown fields rather than rejecting; added policy above.
- Data infra (2025-01-30): requested explicit manifest for dropped fields so joins in analytics remain explainable — added legacy_envelope manifest requirement.
- SDK lead (2025-02-03): requested sample SDK handshake library and a compatibility shim for older Node versions — action item below.

Open questions:
- Do we expose handshake to third-party customers in Private deployments or keep it Console-internal? (security/privacy implications).
- Should the handshake response be signed (HMAC) for on-prem collectors to prevent spoofing?
- How long to honor rollforward window for abandoned collectors? Proposed: 180 days after last heartbeat.

- [SDK leads] Add handshake client to js and python SDKs with a cached policy and fallback behavior (tracking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/589).
- [Data infra] Add ingestion-side field-drop manifest parsing and dashboard queries (tracking ticket ENG-84120).
- [QA] Add end-to-end harness in cicd stage (tracking doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Telemetry/Handshake+E2E+Plan).

Acceptance criteria:
- Handshake endpoint deployed behind a feature flag in canary shard.
- JS and Python SDKs implement handshake + fallback and pass integration tests.
- Data infra ingest accepts versioned_envelope and records manifest for dropped fields.
- Dashboards created and show <0.5% schema_reject_rate after canary period.

If any of the above acceptance criteria fail during canary, we will automatically roll back to legacy_envelope-only by toggling the canary feature flag and convene postmortem.
